newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian party feels pressure ahead of congress.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian party feels pressure ahead of congress.

text.p: Cambodia's unrecognised Khmer Nation Party holds its annual congress this weekend under increasing political pressure and worried about security, party officials said on Friday.

Outspoken KNP leader Sam Rainsy said the party had asked the Interior Ministry to provide extra security during Saturday's congress. "The Cambodian People's Party (CPP) and Hun Sen want to disturb our meeting," he told Reuters on Friday.
The request was expected to be denied.
Two weeks ago, Rainsy announced plans to form an alliance with the royalist Funcinpec party, which currently runs an uneasy coalition government with Cambodia's former communist rulers, the CPP.
The CPP's Hun Sen is co-premier with the Funcinpec's Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Rainsy said intimidation against KNP members had increased in recent weeks as the party gained appeal. It has held rallies and actively supported labour union rights.
"The more popular support the KNP are getting, the more intimidation we are receiving," Rainsy said.
Analysts said KNP's increased activity and looming alliance with Funcinpec had angered the CPP and led to a surge in "dirty politics".
"It seems over recent weeks there has been concerted action to discredit the KNP," said one.
KNP officials denounced a press conference scheduled for late Friday at which a former KNP member was expected to reveal links between the KNP and Khmer Rouge guerrillas.
The Maoist rebels ran the country during the "killing fields" years of 1975 to 1979 during which more than a million Cambodians died through torture, disease or overwork.
"The CPP and Hun Sen are preparing a theatre play to discredit our party and the congress," said a KNP official.
The Khmer Rouge reneged on a 1991 U.N.-sponsored peace pact and have continued to fight the government that was set up after elections in 1993.
But the group has suffered a wave of defections over recent weeks, exacerbating political discord between the coalition partners seeking to woo the former rebels to their side.
